Smooth sedimentation rate curve with uncertainty from a flmw score matrix

Source: R/flmw_path.R
flmw_path.Rd

Turns the sedimentation rate x depth score matrix of flmw into a continuous sedimentation rate curve. The sedimentation rate is not allowed to jump around from one depth to the next: the function finds the most probable path through the score matrix (Viterbi algorithm) and also the probability of every sedimentation rate at every depth (forward-backward algorithm of a hidden Markov model). The probabilities give credible intervals, and prior bounds or known hiatuses can be supplied.

Usage

flmw_path(
  x,
  jump_sd = 0.2,
  sharpness = 3,
  normalize = TRUE,
  sedrate_range = NULL,
  hiatus = NULL,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.16, 0.84, 0.975),
  genplot = FALSE,
  x_lab = "depth",
  y_lab = "sedrate",
  normalise = NULL
)

Arguments

x

Output of flmw (any method), or any list with the elements score_mat (matrix, trial sedimentation rates in rows, depths in columns), depth and y_axis (trial sedimentation rates). Required (no default).

jump_sd

Smoothness of the curve: standard deviation of the relative (natural-log) change in sedimentation rate over 1 metre of depth, scaled with the square root of the depth step (random walk) (numeric, > 0). Small values give a stiff curve, large values let the rate change quickly. Default=0.2.

sharpness

How strongly the score is trusted (numeric, > 0): the likelihood of a sedimentation rate is exp(sharpness * score) with scores between 0 and 1. Lower values give wider credible intervals. Default=3.

normalize

Divide the scores by their 99th percentile (and cap them at 1) so that sharpness means the same for every flmw method (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=TRUE.

sedrate_range

Prior bounds c(min, max) of the sedimentation rate in cm/kyr (numeric vector of length 2): trial rates outside this range are excluded. NULL uses all trial rates. Default=NULL.

hiatus

Depths of hiatuses or other known breaks, in the depth unit of x (numeric vector). At these depths the sedimentation rate may jump freely. NULL means no breaks. Default=NULL.

probs

Cumulative probabilities of the credible interval limits that are returned for every depth (numeric vector, values between 0 and 1). Default=c(0.025, 0.16, 0.84, 0.975) (95 and 68 percent intervals).

genplot

Plot the posterior probability of the sedimentation rate against depth with the most probable path (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

x_lab

Label of the x-axis (depth) of the plot (character). Default="depth".

y_lab

Label of the y-axis (sedimentation rate) of the plot (character). Default="sedrate".

normalise

British spelling of normalize (logical, TRUE or FALSE); if given (not NULL) it overrides normalize. Default=NULL.

Value

A list with depth, y_axis (trial sedimentation rates), path (most probable sedimentation rate curve), mean (posterior mean), interval (matrix with the credible interval limits for every depth), posterior (matrix of probabilities, rates x depths) and score_mat.

Examples

# synthetic score matrix with a gradual change in sedimentation rate
depth <- seq(0, 20, by = 0.1)
rates <- seq(1, 6, by = 0.25)
true_rate <- 2 + 3 * depth / 20
score <- outer(rates, true_rate, function(r, t) exp(-0.5 * ((r - t) / 0.4)^2))
set.seed(1)
score <- pmin(pmax(score + matrix(rnorm(length(score), 0, 0.2), nrow(score)), 0), 1)
fake <- list(score_mat = score, depth = depth, y_axis = rates)
res <- flmw_path(fake)
head(res$path)
#> [1] 2 2 2 2 2 2
